title: Mississippi grocery store encounter
summary: On the morning before the accident, a drunk white man with a pistol made him dance, then gave him a drink and a dollar.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That same morning when I was pulling out, there's a little grocery store that was next to the lot where we were parked. We had a bus where the couples stayed. There was, let's see, one, two, three, four, five, six, eight couples that stayed on this bus. They opened the bus up and made compartments for two couples around here and then two up here and so forth to keep from going around looking for rooms
Well, this man next door at the grocery store, a white fellow next door, he told me that he kind of opened the store early that morning before we left so we could get cigarettes

I went up on the porch, you know, a little porch. The man had the light in the store and I wanted to knock on the door so he could open up, you see, let me in. So here come a fellow, a white fellow, you know, he come along there like he was drunk, you know, a man, he wobbling all around so he wanted to know what I was doing up there. So I told him I was waiting for the man to open the door for me to come in and get something to eat. He told me to get away from there. I said, well, I mean, I'm with the show. And he said, oh, you're with the show? I said, yeah. He said, you dance, huh? I said, no, I'm not a dancer. I said, I'm a musician, a drummer. He said, all you people can dance, all you kind of people can dance. I said, you're going to dance this morning.
Yeah, I've heard people like that.
you know, and he shot down in the floor, you know. Man, you ought to see me dancing. I danced that morning.

So he had a pipe, one of the four pints, he had drank some out of it, you know. Only then he told me to take a drink. Well, I mean, I take my drink and he drank behind me, you know what I mean? And he told me to go ahead and keep the rest of it and give me a dollar for dancing.
That's Mississippi for you. Well, now, he drank behind me. He wanted, you know, he was shooting me, but he still knows. He drank behind me. I don't know. You can't figure what people's on. I've done.
